setup_summary.text: FY2026 (year ended July 31, 2026) revenue was $11.48B, up 24.5% from $9.22B. GAAP operating income fell 44% to $695M, a 6.1% margin versus 13.5% a year earlier.

GAAP and non-GAAP are far apart. Derived Q4 GAAP net income was a loss of $282.4M (-8.3% margin). Separately, full-year FY2026 results included a $620M fair-value loss on the CyberArk 2030 convertible notes and a $58M capped-call gain. Management's Q4 non-GAAP EPS was $1.02, $0.04 above the top of guidance, with non-GAAP operating margin of 29.6%.

Headline growth is flattered by M&A. CyberArk and Chronosphere added $930M of revenue (and an $797M operating loss) after their close dates. The 10-K's unaudited pro forma revenue is $12.31B for FY26 vs $10.49B for FY25, about 17% pro forma growth (derived), against 24.5% reported.

The FY27 guide implies slower like-for-like growth. Revenue of $14.1B-$14.2B against pro forma FY26 revenue of $12.31B is roughly 15% (derived), versus 23%-24% on a reported basis. NGS ARR grew 63% to $9.1B at FY26 year-end and is guided to grow 22%-23% in FY27.

Fiscal Q1 2027 guidance is revenue of $3.30B-$3.31B (33%-34% growth), NGS ARR of $9.54B-$9.56B, RPO of $20.8B-$20.9B and non-GAAP EPS of $0.96-$0.98. The latest consensus (Finnhub) is revenue of $3.37B and EPS of $0.99, above the top of both guided ranges. Consensus revenue implies about 36% growth on $2.47B a year earlier.

The stock arrives at a high bar. Press reports it rose about 14% in the week to Oct 29, after jumping about 6% on Oct 23 on an Evercore channel survey showing stronger cyber demand. It traded at about 85x forward earnings, with estimates already at the top of guidance. Market cap was about $319B.

Fortinet's Q3 (reported Oct 28-30) is a positive firewall and SASE read-across, though a proxy only. Billings rose 29%, product revenue 37%, SASE firewall billings 31% and $1M+ deals 51%. Fortinet shares still fell on the print, which shows how high the sector bar is.

The report date is not confirmed. Finnhub lists Nov 12 (time unknown), while press says mid-to-late November. The average closing move over the last 8 reports is about ±5.1%. No options-implied move or whisper is available yet.

since_filing.text: Shares rallied hard into the print. They rose about 6% on Oct 23 on the Evercore channel survey (CrowdStrike and Okta also rose) and about 7% toward $387 on Oct 26. Press says they were up about 14% over the week to Oct 29 and about 114% YTD as of Oct 28.
The Evercore survey and Gartner's $215B 2026 enterprise cyber budget estimate point to strengthening demand. This is sentiment and channel data, not PANW disclosure.

Fortinet reported Q3 on Oct 28-30. Billings were $2.34B (+29%), revenue $2.08B (+20%), product revenue +37% and SASE firewall billings +31%. It raised full-year billings guidance for the third time, but shares fell. Pricing was described as stabilized, with costs still rising.

Unit 42 said on Oct 29 that the PHP2Shell chain, paired with a Linux kernel flaw, is being exploited against PAN-OS management interfaces. Any support or remediation cost and customer-sentiment impact is unquantified. The 10-K separately disclosed a May 2026 PAN-OS authentication bypass.

Product and partner announcements carried no financial terms. On Oct 23, Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense and Prisma AIRS were listed on the OpenAI Marketplace. On Oct 21, a joint agentic-AI security blog with NVIDIA was published.
On Oct 30, PANW recommended that stockholders reject a Tutanota mini-tender for up to 250,000 shares (about 0.03% of shares) at $450. It is financially immaterial.

Consensus data conflict and should not be mixed. Finnhub shows Q1 EPS of $0.99 and revenue of $3.37B. Press cited $0.93 and $3.22B at the time of guidance. Barchart shows $0.52 diluted EPS for the quarter and FY27 EPS of $2.32, versus company non-GAAP FY27 guidance of $4.16-$4.19.

Sell-side sentiment is bullish, with 40 of 56 analysts at Strong Buy, but the average target of $402.10 (Barchart) implies marginal upside. No dated rating or target change inside the last 14 days could be confirmed.

key_debates.question: Is the beat bar already priced in after a 14% weekly run?

bull.text: Management guides expecting to beat consensus, and the Q4 EPS beat was $0.04 above the top of the range. Peers (Fortinet) and channel checks show strong demand, and bookings accelerated for a second straight quarter.

bear.text: Consensus already sits above the top of the Q1 guide on revenue and EPS. The stock was at about 85x forward earnings with estimates at the top of guidance. Fortinet fell on a beat-and-raise.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q1 revenue versus $3.37B and non-GAAP EPS versus $0.99. Then the size of the beat on NGS ARR above $9.56B, and whether FY27 guidance is raised.

key_debates.question: How much of the growth and ARR is organic or durable?

bull.text: Idira bookings grew faster than revenue in Q4, and $5M+ deals rose 50%. XSIAM ARR grew 70% and observability ARR more than doubled since the Chronosphere close. Platformized-cohort net revenue retention exceeds 120%.

bear.text: Reported 24.5% growth compares with about 17% pro forma, and the FY27 guide implies about 15% pro forma. Q4 net new ARR included a nine-figure single-customer Chronosphere migration that fades in Q1. The 10-K flags usage-optimization risk in AI-native cohorts.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Net new NGS ARR excluding the LLM migration, the Idira growth rate against the high-teens to 20% guide, and observability ARR growth.

key_debates.question: Can margins hold as SaaS mix, hosting and memory costs rise?

bull.text: FY27 non-GAAP operating margin is guided to 29.5% (FY26: 29.2%). Management expects operating leverage and synergies, running three to six months ahead of plan, to more than offset COGS.

bear.text: GAAP gross margin fell 300 bps to 70.4% and GAAP operating margin to 6.1%. Cloud hosting is expected to grow faster than revenue, memory costs persist, and $8.3B of non-cancelable purchase commitments are mostly cloud.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q1 non-GAAP gross margin versus 74.8% in Q4 and the operating margin trend against the 29.5% full-year guide.

key_debates.question: Is the firewall and SASE cycle strong enough to carry Network & AI Security beyond low double digits?

bull.text: SASE bookings grew 40% in FY26 and about $450M of TCV was displaced from competitors, up from $200M at Q3. Software firewall ARR grew 29%, and Fortinet's product revenue grew 37%.

bear.text: Network & AI Security revenue is guided to only low double digits after +17% in FY26. Customers prefer phased multi-year transformations, and Fortinet reports price increases flattening while component costs rise.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Commentary on hardware and SASE bookings, NGFW product revenue growth and pricing.

triggers: NGS ARR near the low end of $9.54B
PAN-OS exploit cost or churn commentary

claim.text: The PAN-OS exploitation campaign is new risk. On Oct 29, Unit 42 said the PHP2Shell chain is being exploited against PAN-OS management interfaces. In May 2026 the company disclosed an authentication bypass in PAN-OS. Reputation, support and remediation costs, and customer concerns about firewall security are unquantified.

Chronosphere ARR is skewed by a single large AI customer. Q4 net new ARR included a nine-figure migration benefit. The 10-K flags usage optimization by AI-native cohorts as a source of revenue volatility.
Gross margin is pressured by acquired-intangible amortization ($640M in FY26; $1.08B in FY27), cloud hosting costs and a global memory shortage that raised hardware costs in Q4.

The 2030 convertible notes and capped calls create GAAP volatility and a possible cash need. The notes are exchangeable at about $211.24 per share, and the conversion trigger is $280.75. Principal of $1.1B would be settled in cash on conversion. The condition was not met in the June quarter, and whether it was met in the September quarter is not confirmed.

Distribution and integration concentration. Two distributors were 30% of FY26 revenue, and one was 19% of gross receivables. Headcount rose 36%, with about 4,223 added from CyberArk. CyberArk (6% of revenue) was excluded from the ICFR assessment.
New competitive threats are flagged in the 10-K: hyperscalers and frontier AI labs entering security and observability, plus market perception that AI could commoditize cybersecurity.
Valuation and sentiment risk. The stock trades at about 84-85x forward earnings after a rapid rise, and consensus already sits above the guide.

questions_for_management.question: How much of Q1 net new NGS ARR and revenue comes from the large LLM customer's Chronosphere migration, and what is organic net new ARR ex-migration?

why.text: The migration lifted Q4 by a nine-figure amount. It tails off in Q1, which management says will be larger than normal. The quality of the ARR beat depends on the organic number.

questions_for_management.question: Why is Q1 RPO guided to $20.8B-$20.9B, below year-end's $21.2B, and what is cRPO expected to do?

why.text: Q1 RPO guidance is below the year-end balance while growth is guided at 34%-35%. Duration and billing mix are the likely drivers.

questions_for_management.question: The Street is above the top of your Q1 revenue and EPS guide. How should we think about the typical size of the beat versus guidance?

why.text: Consensus of $3.37B and $0.99 sits above the guided ranges, while management says it guides to exceed consensus.

questions_for_management.question: What is the commercial and cost impact of the PAN-OS exploitation reported on Oct 29, and has any customer sentiment or pipeline shifted?

why.text: Unit 42 reports active exploitation of PAN-OS management interfaces, and a May 2026 authentication bypass was already disclosed.

questions_for_management.question: How do memory and storage costs, pricing and cloud hosting flow through Q1 and FY27 gross margin, and is there a hardware pricing action planned?

why.text: Management expects hosting to grow faster than revenue and memory costs to persist. Fortinet says price increases are flattening while costs rise.

questions_for_management.question: Is the 2030 notes sale-price condition met, and what is the plan for cash settlement of the $1.1B principal?

why.text: The $280.75 trigger is far below recent trading levels, and cash settlement of principal would follow conversion. The 10-K says the notes were not convertible only because the June-quarter condition was unmet.

questions_for_management.question: What are the like-for-like growth rates for Idira and observability, and when does Chronosphere become competitive in enterprise accounts?

why.text: Pro forma growth is about 17% (FY26) and the FY27 guide implies about 15%, against a reported 23%-24%.
